_meta.provenance: These figures are third-party transcriptions of Forza Horizon 6's own in-game stats panel, published by forza.labsgg.com. They are not first-party Playground Games data and they are not independent measurements. Treat them as a transcription of what the game displays, with the transcriber's rounding.
_meta.howCollected: The car index at /cars embeds the complete dataset as Astro island props in the served HTML; it was read in one request. Every one of the 634 cars was then cross-checked field by field against its own detail page, fetched at roughly one request per second.
_meta.indexVersusDetailPages: All 634 detail pages returned HTTP 200 and matched the index exactly on every numeric field, on PI, drivetrain, price, rarity, car type and year, to the precision the detail page displays. The only differences found were cosmetic: detail pages title-case the manufacturer (BMW renders as Bmw) and title-case the model name, while the index carries the canonical casing used here.
_meta.unitNotes: Raw values are imperial exactly as published. The in-game metric panel labels the same tests 97, 161 and 193 km/h, which are 60, 100 and 120 mph converted; the tests are identical, only the label differs. Lateral g is quoted at 60 and 120 mph, while braking and acceleration are quoted at 60 and 100 mph.

conversionFactors.note: Conversions are unrounded; the raw imperial value is always kept alongside.

fieldNotes.sourceRecord: The verbatim index record for the car, every key exactly as the site publishes it, so nothing is lost to renaming.
fieldNotes.sourceRecord.defaultFrontDisplacement: Unlabelled on the site's own key. It is front weight distribution as a percentage, surfaced here as frontWeightPct; the detail page labels it Front %.
fieldNotes.sourceRecord.manufacturerIndex: Null on every one of the 634 cars.
fieldNotes.sourceRecord.manufacturerVehicleIndex: Null on every one of the 634 cars.
fieldNotes.sourceRecord.createdAt: Site record creation, epoch milliseconds as a string.
fieldNotes.sourceRecord.updatedAt: Site record last update, epoch milliseconds as a string.
fieldNotes.piClass: Read from the detail page chip. The site derives it from PI with the bands D <= 400, C <= 500, B <= 600, A <= 700, S1 <= 800, S2 <= 900, R above 900. These are FH6 bands and they are not the FH5 ones.
fieldNotes.specStatus: complete: all ten simulation fields present. below-test-speed: the only absent figures are 0-100 mph and 100-0 braking on a car whose top speed is under 100 mph, or the 60 mph pair on a car whose top speed is under 60 mph; the site renders these as N/A and the game reports them as failed runs, so they are data rather than gaps. no-specs: an index placeholder with no stats block at all.

knownSourceDefects: 1983 Ford F-150 Forza Edition: 0-60 mph 11.571 s but 0-100 mph 4.700 s.
1989 Nissan S-Cargo Forza Edition: 0-60 mph 17.336 s but 0-100 mph 9.083 s.
2020 Wuling Sunshine S Forza Edition: 0-60 mph 15.746 s but 0-100 mph 7.367 s.

In all three the 0-100 mph figure is faster than the 0-60 mph figure, which is impossible. The detail pages carry the same numbers, so the defect is upstream in the source, not in this scrape. All three are Forza Editions of very slow base cars; the 0-60 figure looks like the unmodified car's. Do not calibrate on them.
2000 Nissan Skyline GT-R V-Spec II: disagrees with the maintainer's own hand-read panel on every field except power and torque. See forza-telemetry.md.
